excerpt: Introducing the llama.cpp benchmark dashboard for AMD Ryzen and Radeon The llama.cpp × AMD Benchmark dashboard is available on Hugging Face. It lets you track prompt processing and text generation performance across llama.cpp builds, models, and quantizations, so you can explore how local inference performs on AMD Ryzen and Radeon hardware. Local inference performance changes as models, kernels, and builds evolve. We want those changes to be easy to inspect for any AMD developer: pick a hardware, a model and a build, compare quantizations, and follow performance over time. The benchmark workflow and underlying results are public, so you can also inspect how we benchmark inference performance. Quick start You can choose Hardware, Model, and llama.cpp build in the Configuration sidebar. The current hardware choices are Radeon 8060S (gfx1151) and Radeon AI Pro R9700S (gfx1201). - In the Overview tab, compare quantizations for one hardware, model, and build. The two charts show PP512 (512 input tokens, no generation) and TG128 (128 generated tokens), both starting at context depth zero. - In the Build history tab, track PP512 and TG128 across all recorded builds for the selected hardware, model, and quantization. - In the Context scaling tab, see how token-generation throughput changes as the existing context grows, for the selected build, hardware, model, and quantization. What the numbers mean The dashboard shows two separate tests, both measured in tokens per second: Both tests start at context depth zero (n_depth=0). PP512 measures processing 512 input tokens without generation; TG128 measures generating 128 tokens without a pre-existing context. The plotted value is the mean throughput (avg_ts). These are useful reference workloads, while the Context scaling tab lets you explore token generation throughput as the context grows.
